families.axis: annoyance at being kept waiting → a standing readiness for uncontrolled anger

members.gloss: a disposition to exhibit uncontrolled anger
members.tone: The heaviest charge in the family: not a passing mood but a settled liability to anger that gets out of hand, so attributing it is an accusation about character.

members.gloss: a dislike of anything that causes delay
members.tone: The narrowest fault here - it fastens on one trigger, delay, and so criticises without alleging the loss of control that *temper* does.

members.gloss: harshness of manner
members.tone: Formal, and it locates the fault in bearing and manner rather than in feeling, which makes the condemnation cool and considered.

members.gloss: harshness of manner
members.tone: The plain word for the same harsh manner, felt as a cutting edge on how someone deals with you rather than *asperity*'s formal verdict on them.

families.axis: a plain absence of study → the gap charged as a fault in the person

members.gloss: uneducated in the fundamentals of a given art or branch of learning; lacking knowledge of a specific field
members.tone: Blunt and accusing: the missing fundamentals of one art or branch of learning are laid at the person's door rather than at their schooling's, which is what makes it bite where *untutored* does not.

members.gloss: uneducated in the fundamentals of a given art or branch of learning; lacking knowledge of a specific field
members.tone: Borrows the whole force of being unable to read and drops it on a single field's fundamentals, so a bounded gap in knowledge sounds total — showier scorn than *ignorant*.

members.gloss: lacking in schooling
members.tone: Mild and almost exculpating, since it puts the deficiency in the schooling that was never had rather than in the head that went without it.

members.gloss: lacking knowledge gained by study often in a particular field
members.tone: A flat report that knowledge was not gained by study, with or without a particular field in view, and no reproach travels with it — the coolest word here beside *ignorant*.

families.axis: a bare instance named → an instance the word passes verdict on

members.gloss: a poor example
members.tone: Flatly dismissive - the thing is put forward as an example and judged to fall short of being one.

members.gloss: a poor example
members.tone: Rueful where *excuse* is blunt - the same verdict of inadequacy, delivered with a wince rather than a sneer.

members.gloss: an item of information that is typical of a class or group
members.tone: Neutral, and the instance is offered to make the class visible - explanatory work that *instance* makes no claim to.

members.gloss: an item of information that is typical of a class or group
members.tone: The barest of the neutral terms - one case counted off, with none of the demonstrative purpose of *illustration*.

members.gloss: an item of information that is typical of a class or group
members.tone: The plain unmarked word for a typical item, carrying neither the explanatory duty of *illustration* nor the scrutiny of *specimen*.

members.gloss: an instance that does not conform to a rule or generalization
members.tone: Positional rather than evaluative - the instance is defined by not fitting the rule, and the word passes no judgement on it for that.

members.gloss: an example regarded as typical of its class
members.tone: Clinical - the instance is held up and inspected as a stand-in for its class, where *example* merely names it.

members.gloss: an example that is used to justify similar occurrences at a later time
members.tone: Gives the instance forward reach - an example that licenses what comes after it rather than just typifying a group.

families.axis: haste as plain fast movement → haste that turns careless and costs the mover dignity

members.gloss: the act of moving hurriedly and in a careless manner
members.tone: The plainest name for going fast and going badly at once, with the carelessness carried quietly rather than pressed.

members.gloss: the act of moving hurriedly and in a careless manner
members.tone: Puts the weight on momentum - a harder-edged, more headlong version of *hurry*, where the speed is what overrides the care.

members.gloss: the act of moving hurriedly and in a careless manner
members.tone: Formal and weighty, naming the hurry as a fault to be answered for where *hurry* merely reports it.

members.gloss: the act of moving hurriedly and in a careless manner
members.tone: The participle keeps the careless speed running on as an activity rather than a single lapse, unlike the finished act *rush* names.

members.gloss: the act of moving with great haste
members.tone: Great speed as a sudden break away, all abruptness and no blame - the carelessness that shadows *hurry* is absent.

members.gloss: the act of moving with great haste
members.tone: Speed as a short spirited burst, brisk and deliberate beside the startled suddenness of *bolt*.

members.gloss: rushing about hastily in an undignified way
members.tone: Makes the hurry small and skittering, so the loss of dignity comes out as comic rather than damning.

members.gloss: rushing about hastily in an undignified way
members.tone: The undignified hurry as graceless floundering - effortful disorder where *scamper* is merely quick and silly.

families.axis: respectful address for an old woman → old woman rendered ugly and evil

members.gloss: a term of address for an elderly woman
members.tone: A way of speaking to an old woman rather than a way of describing her, and it lends her the standing of kin in the act of addressing her.

members.gloss: an ugly evil-looking old woman
members.tone: Puts menace behind the ugliness - she does not just look evil, she looks capable of it, which is the charge *hag* leaves off.

members.gloss: an ugly evil-looking old woman
members.tone: Repulsion with nothing added: the same ugly, evil-looking figure as *witch* but stripped of any power, so it jeers where *witch* recoils.

members.gloss: an old woman
members.tone: A diminutive fastened to any old woman at all, grandmother or not - familiar where *mother* is deferential, and it shrinks her to her age.

families.axis: politeness kept to its outward form → manners raised to excellence

members.gloss: formal or perfunctory politeness
members.tone: The family's floor: politeness as observed form, either done correctly or gone through with no interest at all, which is why it approves far less warmly than *graciousness*.

members.gloss: courteous regard for people's feelings
members.tone: Aims the courtesy at what another person feels rather than at a code of conduct, so it credits attention where *politeness* credits only correctness.

members.gloss: courtesy towards women
members.tone: Defined by whom the courtesy is shown to — women — so it marks its object where *courtesy* marks only the manner.

members.gloss: a courteous manner
members.tone: The unmarked term for the manner itself, with no standard, object or degree attached; every word beside it adds one of those.

members.gloss: courteous regard for people's feelings
members.tone: The same courteous regard for feelings as *respect*, but with a yielding in it — the regard shows itself by giving way.

members.gloss: a courteous manner that respects accepted social usage
members.tone: The plainest name for conduct that respects accepted usage, so mild that the approval barely registers as praise beside *politeness*.

members.gloss: excellence of manners or social conduct
members.tone: Not merely meeting the standard of manners but excelling at it, which puts it at the top of this family where *civility* sits at the bottom.

families.axis: swelling something past its true size → planting an outright falsehood in a believer

members.gloss: cause someone to believe an untruth
members.tone: Names the act by its result — the untruth has landed and is believed — where *mislead* stops at the information handed over.

members.gloss: cause someone to believe an untruth
members.tone: The same planting of a false belief, but the word frames it as a breach of the trust that made the believing possible, which is what makes it the heaviest term here.

members.gloss: tell an untruth; pretend with intent to deceive
members.tone: Flat and unsoftened, covering both the untruth spoken and the pretence behind it, with no room left for an innocent reading.

members.gloss: give false or misleading information to
members.tone: The gentlest of the deceptions: it charges only the false or misleading information given and leaves intent unsettled, where *lie* settles it.

members.gloss: to enlarge beyond bounds or the truth
members.tone: Makes the thing itself loom larger, so the overreach shows in the size of the picture rather than in a claim stated outright.

members.gloss: to enlarge beyond bounds or the truth
members.tone: The plain charge of overstatement, taking in both going past reasonable bounds and going past the truth, and always implying the real measure is smaller.

members.gloss: to enlarge beyond bounds or the truth
members.tone: Says only that something has been swelled; the fault lies in the going beyond, not in the verb, which is why it accuses least of the three.

families.axis: sufficient for the job → genuinely skilled at it

members.gloss: have the skills and qualifications to do things well
members.tone: The same compliment pitched cooler than *able* — an appraisal of what someone is equipped to do well rather than a warm word for them.

members.gloss: properly or sufficiently qualified or capable or efficient
members.tone: The mildest approval here, since 'properly or sufficiently' sets a threshold and reports it met — qualified, capable or efficient enough, and no claim beyond enough.

members.gloss: able to accomplish a purpose; functioning effectively
members.tone: Approval aimed at the working rather than the worker: the purpose is accomplished and the thing functions, which is a narrower compliment than *able*.

members.gloss: worthy of a good workman
members.tone: Praises by holding the thing up to a standard-bearer — worthy of a good workman — which makes it concrete where *competent* stays abstract.
